rules: BeerJSON analytical-scale tokens are source-format tokens, not FermentationJSON physical-unit identifiers.
The BeerJSON source value and token MUST be preserved even when a native quantity is constructed.

A scale-defined native quantity uses an explicit quantity kind and measurement-scale identifier; its unit is the neutral numeric carrier 'one' unless the BeerJSON token denotes a physical unit such as g/l.
Conversion between distinct measurement scales is a calculation with model/method/reference-condition provenance, not a unit conversion.

An analytical range may become one native range only when both endpoints map to the same native quantity kind and scale; mixed-scale endpoints remain independently preserved unless an explicit conversion is performed.

non_unit_conversion_rules.reason: density/extract relationship depends on an identified table or model and reference conditions.
Brix is a sucrose mass-fraction scale and is not generically identical to wort extract.
Both are method-defined spectrophotometric indices; FermentationJSON does not encode their relationship as a physical-unit conversion.
Lovibond is not treated as equivalent to the modern spectrophotometric beer-color method.
The relationship depends on the definition/reference conditions for the gas volume.
IBU is an operational analytical result and is not an identity with iso-alpha-acid mass concentration.
The scales arise from diastatic-power methods; any conversion must cite the adopted method relationship rather than masquerading as a unit conversion.

range_policy.same_scale: construct_native_range_after validating compatible quantity kind and scale
range_policy.mixed_scale: preserve both BeerJSON endpoint objects; derive a normalized range only through an explicit calculation model
